{{Quote|There's no place like home&mdash;and this isn't it.|Jori Daragon|<ref name="collision" />}}
'''Ronika''' was a [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]], which was used as a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] colony around the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Ronika was the eighth planet in the [[Star system/Legends|system]], and had one [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. First settled around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the harsh landscape was not conducive to settlement; to prepare the planet for large-scale colonization, [[Empress/Legends|Empress]] [[Teta/Legends|Teta]], the ruler of the system, used prison labor to [[Terraforming/Legends|terraform]] Ronika. After the conclusion of the [[Unification Wars (Koros)/Legends|Unification Wars]], many members of the rebels of [[Kirrek]] were imprisoned on Ronika. Later that year, [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] explorer [[Jori Daragon]], convicted of a wide variety of charges, was sent to Ronika. However, intending to warn Teta of the looming [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] threat to invade the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Daragon stole an [[Drone ore shuttle|ore shuttle]] and escaped. Daragon's forebodings proved to be true; just days later the Sith attacked the Republic. Teta appointed [[Llaban]], former leader of the Kirrek rebels to lead a defense [[Army/Legends|army]] on Kirrek, and reinforced his ranks by freeing his former [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] on Ronika. The freed [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] played a large role in a Republic victory in the subsequent [[Battle of Kirrek (Great Hyperspace War)|battle]] at Kirrek.

==Description==
{{Quote|I don't suppose Ronika is much of a resort world.|Jori Daragon|<ref name="collision" />}}
Ronika was the eighth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]], revolving around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Koros]]. Ronika had one [[Moon/Legends|moon]].<ref name="byss" /> The planet had a harsh landscape, dominated by brightly-colored rocky cliffs and desert sands, which caused Ronika to appear [[Color/Legends|red]] from [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. To survive on Ronika, one needed a fully stocked [[survival pack]], including [[allergy paste]]s, [[anti-venom ampule]]s, [[emergency scab bandage]]s, and [[ultraviolet eye shield]]s. The high [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]] levels on the planet and the bright, hot sun required visitors to the planet to stay tightly bundled up at all times. One of the native [[Species/Legends|species]] was the [[stinger moth]], a highly venomous flying insect.<ref name="collision" />

==History==
{{Quote|Prisoner! Halt!|Guards attempt to stop Jori Daragon's escape|<ref name="collision" />}}
Ronika was first settled around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], and was used as a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] colony world by [[Empress/Legends|Empress]] [[Teta/Legends|Teta]], the ruler of the then-Koros [[Star system/Legends|system]]. Teta shipped criminals from the system to Ronika to pay off their debt to society by preparing the arid world for large-scale settlement. That year, rebels on the planet [[Kirrek]] fought against [[Koros fleet|Teta's military]] in the [[Battle of Kirrek (Unification Wars)|Battle of Kirrek]]. After their defeat, many of the rebels were sentenced to labor on Ronika,<ref name="cswe" /> where they worked smashing rocks and collecting the valuable [[Ore/Legends|ore]] inside. Later in 5000 BBY, [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] explorer [[Jori Daragon]] was sent to Ronika after being arrested on an outstanding record and convicted. Daragon was desperate to leave as her brother, [[Gav Daragon]], had been captured by the long-isolated [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]]; also, Daragon had discovered [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow's]] ambitions to invade the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. However, her protests and warnings fell on deaf ears and Daragon hatched a plan to escape from the planet.<ref name="collision" />

Spontaneously falling to the ground, Jori Daragon cried out that one of the native stinger moths had stung her, distracting the guards who came to assist her. As the guards left their posts to help, Daragon sprang up off the ground and stole one of the [[Drone ore shuttle]]s that were on the planet collecting ore. An experienced [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], Daragon was able to keep pursuing [[Starship/Legends|ships]] at bay until she reached [[Empress Teta/Legends|Koros Major's]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Cinnagar/Legends|Cinnagar]]. Although the guard ships destroyed the [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], Daragon safely ejected and was able to warn Teta of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] threat.<ref name="collision" /> Daragon's forebodings proved true when, just a few days later, [[Sith invasion fleet|Naga Sadow's invasion force]] [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|attacked]] the Republic. With a part of Sadow's force poised to attack the Koros system, Teta enlisted [[Llaban]], former leader of the rebels on Kirrek, to command a defense army in a battle for Kirrek. Teta also promised to free some of his former rebel [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] on Ronika to aid him.<ref name="encounter">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref> Teta kept her promise, and the freed [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] from Ronika proved pivotal in the Koros victory in the [[Battle of Kirrek (Great Hyperspace War)|Battle of Kirrek]]. Eventually the Republic was victorious in the war.<ref name="dogs">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 4]]</ref>

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] [[Eara Lota/Legends|Eara Lota]], the niece of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Alor Keto/Legends|Alor Keto]] and heir to the throne of [[Empress Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]], protested the conditions that prisoners of Ronika were forced to endure. She was frequently seen on localized [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]] attempting to spread her message.<ref name="Nexus of Power">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Sometimes I wonder if the courts are eager to sentence war criminals just to have cheap workers for their colony planets.|Jori Daragon|<ref name="collision" />}}
Upon first settlement, Ronika was not suitable for large-scale colonization, due to the arid climate, harsh environment, and poisonous native species. In order to prepare Ronika for settlers, the Koros government brought many criminals to the planet to help [[Terraforming/Legends|terraform]] Ronika's surface.<ref name="cswe" /> The prisoners were not allowed to leave the planet, and were constantly watched by guards. At regular intervals, drone shuttles came to the planet to collect ore that the prisoners had extracted from the rocks.<ref name="collision" />

==Locations==
{{Quote|I gotta get out of this place.|Jori Daragon|<ref name="collision" />}}
Ronika was a very barren world, with little but cliffs and deserts. Several large man-made structures could be seen on the planet, however. Also, there were several large clearings to accommodate landing ore ships.<ref name="collision" />

==Behind the scenes==
The planet Ronika first appeared in ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire]]'', a story arc of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series, written by [[Kevin J. Anderson]] and released in [[1997]]. Ronika only directly appears in the arc's second issue, [[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 2|''Forces in Collision'']], where it was illustrated by [[Dario Carrasco, Jr.]]<ref name="collision" /> However, the planet was later mentioned in the third issue, [[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''First Encounter'']],<ref name="encounter" /> and the fourth issue, [[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''The Dogs of War'']].<ref name="dogs" /> More information on the planet was given in the [[2005]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement ''[[Byss and the Deep Core]]'',<ref name="byss" /> and in [[2008]], Ronika was given an entry in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="cswe" /> A continuity issue was raised by ''Byss and the Deep Core''; in ''Forces in Collision'', Ronika is shown as being in a [[Binary star/Legends|binary star]] system, but ''Byss and the Deep Core'' places Ronika in the Empress Teta system, which has just one star. However, ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' confirmed that Ronika was in the Empress Teta system.
